log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought:
The opponent has Dragonite, Gholdengo, Mimikyu, Garchomp, Volcarona and Primarina. Dragon, Ghost, Fairy and Fire threats are common among them.

Kingambit handles Mimikyu, Gholdengo and Primarina well and resists Dragon. Dragapult is fast and hits Dragonite, Garchomp and the Ghost types. Gholdengo threatens Volcarona and Dragonite, though Garchomp's Rock Slide is useful against Volcarona too. Incineroar is a solid lead with Fake Out and Intimidate, but Kingambit already covers the Fairy and Ghost types, so I'll take Garchomp for speed and Mega power.

I'll bring Dragapult for speed, Kingambit for the Ghost and Fairy matchups, and Garchomp for coverage against Volcarona and Dragonite.
Volcarona threatens their Steel-heavy core, Primarina handles opposing Dragons and Incineroar, and Garchomp applies immediate offensive pressure.

I outspeed Garchomp (213 vs at most 169). Draco Meteor is super effective with Life Orb and should do big damage, likely close to a knockout. Garchomp's Dragon moves and Earthquake are threats, but I move first. Shadow Ball is safer but does much less damage. Draco Meteor's 90% accuracy is acceptable here.
Dragapult easily outspeeds Garchomp and threatens an immediate Dragon-type knockout. Switching to Primarina is safe due to its Fairy typing granting complete immunity to Dragon moves.

Primarina is Water/Fairy and Draco Meteor can't touch it. Dragapult outspeeds it comfortably, and Shadow Ball is neutral and strong with Life Orb. It will chip Primarina heavily while I stay ahead on speed. Primarina's Moonblast would only do neutral damage to me, so staying in is fine.
Dragapult is at -2 Sp. Atk after Draco Meteor and cannot threaten Primarina. STAB Moonblast easily OHKOs Dragapult or heavily dents any potential switch-in.

Primarina is Water/Fairy, so Kingambit's Dark and Steel moves are weak to its Fairy typing: Dark is resisted and Steel is neutral... Steel hits Fairy super effectively, and Iron Head also flinches. Kingambit resists Fairy, since Steel resists it, so Moonblast does little. Kingambit is the safer switch-in and Iron Head threatens heavy damage. Garchomp is weak to Fairy, and Moonblast would hurt it badly.

Primarina is Water/Fairy, so Iron Head (Steel) is super effective against Fairy and neutral against Water, which makes it the best coverage move. Kingambit has one fainted ally, so it gets a 10% boost. Primarina is at 68% and will likely outspeed and hit with Moonblast, which Kingambit resists as a Dark/Steel type. Iron Head does solid damage and may flinch.
Kingambit will likely click Iron Head or Kowtow Cleave; Volcarona easily resists Steel and threatens an OHKO with Fiery Dance while threatening Flame Body.

Volcarona is at 55% and faster than Kingambit. Sucker Punch has priority and hits for neutral damage with a 1.1x Overlord boost. Volcarona's likely attacks (Fiery Dance, Bug Buzz, Quiver Dance, etc.) are all damaging or setup, and Sucker Punch fails only if it uses a status move like Quiver Dance. Kowtow Cleave never misses and deals more damage, but it hits after Volcarona moves. Sucker Punch probably knocks it out first, since Volcarona is at 55% and weak to nothing Dark but takes neutral damage; Kingambit at 205 Atk should do roughly 40-50% to it. It's close, but priority matters most here.

Volcarona naturally outspeeds Kingambit and Fiery Dance is super effective, dealing massive damage or knocking it out. Even if Kingambit uses Sucker Punch, Volcarona survives from 55% HP and consumes Sitrus Berry.
Garchomp is at full HP, naturally outspeeds Kingambit, and threatens an immediate knockout with STAB Earthquake.
Mega Garchomp easily survives a Supreme Overlord Sucker Punch from full HP and secures a guaranteed OHKO with Earthquake.

Garchomp likely outspeeds Kingambit and Earthquake hits it hard, but Kingambit should survive one. Sucker Punch's priority guarantees I deal damage before each Earthquake and gets in two hits. If Garchomp attacks, Sucker Punch is better than the slower Kowtow Cleave. Switching into my own Garchomp is a speed gamble, so I'll attack.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Only Dragapult has fainted so far, and Volcarona belongs to the opponent. Garchomp is at full health and could mega evolve, but Kingambit's Dark-type moves are neutral against its Dragon/Ground typing, so Kowtow Cleave with its boosted power is still a solid neutral option. I'm also weighing that Garchomp likely carries Earthquake, which would hit Kingambit's Steel typing hard.

Running the numbers, Kowtow Cleave does roughly 50% to Garchomp, meaning two hits are needed to KO it, while Garchomp's Earthquake could do close to that much back to Kingambit plus Rough Skin chip damage on contact. If Garchomp outspeeds and has Sucker Punch too, I'm worried Kingambit loses the damage race since two Earthquakes could kill before I land my second Kowtow Cleave.

I'm also weighing switching to my own Garchomp for a mirror matchup, but speed tiers and mega availability are uncertain enough that this feels like a coinflip rather than a safe play.

Thinking through sequencing instead: if I lead with Sucker Punch, priority lets me chip damage before it moves, but two hits still likely leave it short of a kill given Rough Skin recoil working against me too. If I use Kowtow Cleave instead, I eat an Earthquake first but could still land two solid hits — though I risk dying before my second attack goes off, so the exact turn order really matters here.

Two Sucker Punches gets me to about 80% total damage but doesn't secure the kill, and Rough Skin chips me down each time I connect, so a mega or Garchomp switch doesn't really change the math since it comes down to speed. Kowtow Clause hits harder but is slower, while Sucker Punch guarantees priority damage twice regardless of their move — I'll go with Sucker Punch.

decisions.thought: Mega Garchomp easily survives another Sucker Punch from Kingambit (took ~39% last turn, currently at 60.7%). Earthquake guarantees the knockout.

Kingambit is at 13% and slower, so it will almost certainly die to Earthquake this turn. Sucker Punch goes first and takes Garchomp from 60% to about 20%. That chip lets my own full-health Garchomp finish it easily when it comes in. The risk is that the opponent switches to Primarina and Sucker Punch fails, which is acceptable.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Kingambit at 27 HP and Garchomp at 60%, another Sucker Punch would only bring it to 20%, not a knockout, so I'm checking how many allies have fainted so far — just Dragapult it seems.

Switching to my own Garchomp is tempting since it's not mega-evolved yet and could outspeed this weakened Mega Garchomp, but I need to weigh whether Protect buys anything useful here versus just trading Kingambit for chip damage before it faints to Earthquake.

Sucker punch trades Kingambit at low HP for guaranteed chip, then Garchomp comes in fresh against a weakened Garchomp. The risk is opponent switching to Primarina to dodge the sucker punch, but that's an acceptable outcome, so I'll go with sucker punch.

decisions.thought: Kingambit fainted, so I must send in my only remaining Pokémon, Garchomp. It is at full health against a Garchomp on 22% HP, and it can knock that one out.

Opposing Garchomp is at 22% and is Mega Evolved. Mega Evolving boosts my Speed, so I'll move first either way. Dragon Claw is super effective and should easily knock it out. Mega Evolving also adds power, so I'll use it.

Opposing Garchomp likely outspeeds Mega Garchomp and will attempt to KO it, but switching Primarina into an Earthquake is too risky. Firing off Outrage guarantees massive damage or a KO if they lack Speed investment, leaving Primarina in a safe position to clean up.

Primarina is Water/Fairy, so Dragon Claw has no effect. Earthquake is neutral and Rock Slide is super effective against Water, though Rock Slide is only 75 power at 90% accuracy. Mega Garchomp is faster, so I move first.

Earthquake with Sand Force is not boosted, since there is no sand. Mega Garchomp has Sand Force and becomes Sand Force, but there is no sandstorm. Earthquake does neutral damage with 100 power, while Rock Slide is 75 power and 2x against Water, so it does more.

Rock Slide is the stronger option: 75 x 2 = 150 effective power vs 100, with a flinch chance and a 90% accuracy cost. Primarina has 68% HP, so Rock Slide is likely to KO or come close.

Mega Garchomp is weak to Fairy, making Moonblast the strongest and most reliable attack to secure the knockout and win the match. Primarina's Fairy typing provides immunity to Dragon Claw, giving it the best shot to survive and retaliate.
